body.x: Inside a single robot, camera and LiDAR perception, AI decisions and motor control all run at once, each on its own cycle. If that flow arrives slightly late or out of order, the robot moves inaccurately or stops.

Intellectus Corp., a Seoul-based company founded in 2020 and led by CEOs Seongyu Ko and Seongwook Kim, builds integrated middleware to manage that flow. At KES 2026, it is presenting int2ConneX in the DIPS Future Mobility Pavilion, and it plans to attend the KES Innovation Awards ceremony on Oct. 13. int2ConneX received a KES 2026 Innovation Award. The company wants to find robotics, mobility and defense partners to validate it.

The core of int2ConneX is int2DDS, a Data Distribution Service (DDS) engine the company built in Rust on the international standard from the Object Management Group (OMG). int2ConneX separates heavy AI inference from real-time control so that AI workloads do not delay control. It can swap AI models without stopping the robot, deploy software remotely with automatic rollback and work with existing ROS 2-based robot software. It also manages where software runs separately from what runs, so software developed on a single PC can move to a robot or vehicle with several computers by changing the deployment rather than the code. It supports real-time inference and training-data collection at the same time, so models can keep improving with data gathered in operation.

The company says int2ConneX is being evaluated in robotics, defense and manufacturing AI. It has delivered the platform to LIG D&A for a project that standardizes the communication layer among different unmanned systems and is carrying out a defense research project with Hyundai Rotem. In August 2025, it registered as a DDS vendor with the OMG, and it takes part in AUTOSAR as a development partner. int2DDS and its ROS 2 integration layer, rmw_int2dds, are open source, and in 2026 the company presented them at ROSCon in Toronto and the OMG Technical Meeting in Orlando. Its awards include a Minister of Science and ICT Award and a KISA President's Award.

Intellectus expects 2026 revenue of about KRW 4.0 billion (about USD 2.9 million) and has raised about KRW 6.0 billion in total investment. int2ConneX has no formal export record, but the company has carried out overseas projects in China, Southeast Asia and Europe and is working with Chinese industrial software company Yonyou on a project for a Korean steel maker.

The United States and Europe are its target markets, because DDS is widely used in defense and robotics there and both have large ROS 2 developer communities. It is looking for robot and mobility makers to build in int2ConneX, system integrators and defense companies that need a standards-based communication layer for unmanned systems. It is pursuing a Korean software quality certification in 2026 and an international functional safety certification in 2027, and plans a booth at ROSCon Korea in early 2027. The company names the cost and lead time of international certification, the lack of overseas references and the cost of working in standards bodies such as the OMG and AUTOSAR as its main challenges.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event features X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
